overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the evidence did not show Board members deliberated on the complainant's license outside a posted meeting. Non-OML concerns were not reviewed. A reminder about pre-meeting discussion was given, not an order.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged two Board members discussed his license application before the March 18 meeting began, outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that there is insufficient evidence to support a finding that the Board deliberated outside of a posted meeting

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a pre-meeting draft license implied the Board deliberated on his license before the meeting, contrary to normal practice.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, agreement among public body members or taking action with little discussion is insufficient to support the inference that members deliberated outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant also raised concerns about Board members' behavior at the meeting and the licensing process, which are not Open Meeting Law matters.
allegations.key_passage: These matters do not fall within the scope of the Open Meeting Law and we do not address them in this determination.
